entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sancha of Portugal (c. 1178-13 Mar 1229) was a Portuguese infanta, second daughter of King Sancho I of Portugal and Dulce of Aragon.

As the sister of Afonso II, Sancha played a crucial role in the politics of the Kingdom of Portugal during the early 13th century. Her marriage to Henry III, Count of Provence, solidified alliances with powerful European nobles and furthered her family's interests.

Sancha's influence extended beyond her royal connections; she was also an accomplished patron of the arts, supporting scholars and artists in Lisbon and other Portuguese cities. Her legacy as a shrewd politician and cultural leader has endured for centuries, cementing her place among the most fascinating figures of medieval Portugal.

The passing of Sancha of Portugal in 1229 marked the end of an era for the Kingdom of Portugal, but her impact on European politics and culture would be felt for generations to come.
